column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls mankind sons of Adam.
The Hebrew names a river and says let us rejoice there; BSB says waters and we rejoiced.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew commands making the sound heard; BSB uses let it be heard.
The Hebrew has our soul and our foot in the singular; BSB has our lives and our feet.
The Hebrew repeats the refining root in the comparison with silver; BSB simply says like silver.
The Hebrew names pressure on our loins; BSB has burdens on our backs.
The Hebrew has a singular man riding over our heads; BSB has men.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the lips opening; BSB says they promised vows.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says what He did for my soul; BSB says for me.
The Hebrew says exaltation was under my tongue; BSB describes actively praising Him with the tongue.
The Hebrew says seeing iniquity in the heart; BSB says cherishing it.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses not turning away for both prayer and loving devotion; BSB uses rejecting the prayer and withholding the devotion.
